The person behind the work

Curious about ideas.
Committed to making them work.

I’m Ming, a computer scientist in Melbourne. I study and build systems that make decisions under changing workloads, incomplete information, and practical resource constraints.

My route into this work began with robots: speech interaction with a NAO robot, then cloud robotics and real-time multi-robot map fusion at the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Working across sensors, networks, and central computing made the system around a learning method just as interesting to me as the method itself.

I later led telecommunications and smart-finance R&D projects at SIAT. That experience connected predictive modeling with operational data, industry requirements, and the work of coordinating a technical team.

During my PhD at the University of Melbourne, I focused on demand prediction and resource management for microservices. I developed forecasting and scheduling methods, implemented research software, and built controlled Kubernetes experiments to examine how those methods behave when conditions change.

I now work part-time on wearable R&D at CyterX, where data quality, timing, and numerical verification remain central questions. Alongside this, I teach and supervise industry-partner data science projects.

The questions I work on

I develop learning methods and software for systems that have to make decisions under changing conditions. My work spans cloud–edge resource management, evidence-based agent workflows, and reproducible ML engineering.

Adaptive cloud & edge systems

How should services scale and move when demand, traffic, and network conditions change together?

Resource forecasting, capacity-constrained placement, telemetry, and controllable experimentation.

iDynamicsTraDEEN-Beats

Evidence-based AI workflows

How can an agent’s assessment remain inspectable when the source information is incomplete or heterogeneous?

Structured criteria, metadata extraction, bounded critique, assessment traces, and evaluation.

AgentFAIR

Reliable ML engineering

What needs to be controlled and checked before a model result becomes useful evidence?

Pinned inputs, modular training software, numerical checks, sensor-data audits, and repeatable experiments.

Transformer trainingWearable R&D

How I approach the work

Start with the decision.

Clarify who needs the result, what action it supports, and which constraints matter.

Build something inspectable.

Keep configurations, interfaces, data assumptions, and experimental records clear enough for another person to examine.

Evaluate the whole system.

Connect algorithm behavior to measurements, implementation costs, and the conditions attached to the conclusion.
